task.pr_title: Fix memory leak and stale-model results when hot-swapping PredictionEnginePool

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
Copilot noticed the PredictionEnginePoolPolicy actually uses this method to create engines:

```csharp
public override PredictionEngine<TData, TPrediction> Create() =>
     _mlContext.Model.CreatePredictionEngine<TData, TPrediction>(_model);
```

it uses this method in turn:

```csharp
public static PredictionEngine<TSrc, TDst> CreatePredictionEngine<TSrc, TDst>(
     this ITransformer transformer,
     IHostEnvironment env,
     bool ignoreMissingColumns = true,
     SchemaDefinition inputSchemaDefinition = null,
     SchemaDefinition outputSchemaDefinition = null,
     bool ownsTransformer = true)
```

note the last parameter `ownsTransformer` having default=true, which means every single engine thinks it owns it and will gladly dispose it when itself disposed. This seems a slumbering bug actually waiting till we fix the issue with disposing. I guess the solution now passes tests because there is one model they consume without sharing with other engines.

evidence.thread_resolution: kotlarmilos: Confirmed and fixed, thanks for catching this. Create() was using the default ownsTransformer of true, so every engine in a generation thought it owned the single shared transformer, and once we actually dispose engines the first disposal tears the model down for its siblings. Engines are now created with OwnsTransformer set to false, and PoolLoader owns the shared model's lifetime per generation, disposing it with the generation and guarded by reference equality so a model still used by the surviving generation is never disposed.
